title: Well folks, I did it!!!  My very first hologram(s)!

posts.topic_title: Well folks, I did it!!!  My very first hologram(s)!
posts.author: Grey
posts.post_subject: Well folks, I did it!!!  My very first hologram(s)!
posts.content_md:
Actually, I should say 'we'. My brother, my girlfriend and myself. We did a total of 5 single-beam exposures, using Slavich 01 film cut into 2 inch pieces, and a D&S laser. We used a cinderblock painted black sitting on 8 pieces of bubblewrap, 2 pieces of glass held together with spring clips and magnets to form a base, a clothespin in a cup of sand sitting on bricks to hold the laser, and a green diode flashlight for the safelight. Our subject was 3 dice arranged in a pyramid. The developer was the JD-2 kit.

The first attempt was a complete disaster... We turned off the lights and sat, waiting for everything to settle down. About a minute later, we realized that we could see each other... quite well in fact. Light was bleeding into the room in all directions. Rather than throw in the towel, we went ahead and exposed for 15 seconds. Then, as I was walking to the table to develop the film, I tripped and fell into the wall. And in an attempt to steady myself, guess where my hand landed? You got it. The light switch. I shut it off as quickly as possible (of course, my partners where doubled over in tears, laughing), and developed the film.

We weren't expecting much, and that's exactly what we got. So, we packed up the setup and put it in the bedroom's walk in closet. My brother and I holed up in there with all the equipment and chemicals (God, it was so hot), and went quickly to work, weathering all the head on collisions with the closet shelving, and each other. This time we exposed for 5 seconds, and developed. Nothing. We decided to take a break, and as I was walking out of the room, I saw something out of the corner of my eye. IT WAS DICE!!! I grabbed the film and ran outside. Sure enough, it was dim, but the image was there! Fueled with excitement, we returned to the closet. This time we exposed for 3 seconds... and we ended up with a much brighter image. Next, we tried 1.5, and this turned out to be perfect. A beautiful set of dice with a wide field of view. Our last experiment was for .5 seconds, with a result similar to the second.

Man, I had no idea this could be so much fun (even screwing up!). This has been a dream of mine since I was 14, wayyyy back in 1978. I can't believe its finally happened!!!

I just wanted to thank you for all the advice you guys gave me. It worked out beautifully. Hopefully, I can get ahold of a decent camera and post a shot soon.

Thanks again,

Mike

posts.author: Grey
posts.post_subject: Well folks, I did it!!!  My very first hologram(s)!
posts.content_md:
Guess what... I was looking at all the holograms for the millionth time last night, when I actually found an image on the first 'ruined' exposure we made (the one in which I turned on the overhead lights). It's very dim, and can only be seen in a dark room with a bright flashlight, but it's there. I'm amazed. Even our worst, most screwed up attempt produced an image. It was really exciting to realize that we succeeded on our first attempt after all (bad as it was). 

But that fourth (1.5 second exposure) we did... Man that thing is beautiful. I can't believe it came from us! 

Needless to say, I didn't sleep much last night, and I dreamed about holograms the whole time. 

Even as I type this, I feel compelled to go look at them, so I think I will... Bye! LOL

Heh, my first hologram was a densiyuk (sp?) of a T-piece BNC network connector. I used to carry it around and show random girls on the bus A good conversation starter.

I was a bit confused at first, and put the film in the developer, then exposed it while it was wet. I can't remember if that worked or not now. I had a window in the ceiling and tried to block it up with whatever I could find, which mostly involved taping chunks of cardboard boxes to the ceiling. It was a real mess.

Ah, the memories of youth. That was back when I still had hair and was young and full of life. (just over a year ago.)

That brings up a question.. We noticed that the ones that were over-exposed were greenish, and the ones that were under-exposed were pretty red. The ones that were best and brightest were kind of an off-white orangey color. I always thought that they would *all* be red, just dimmer or brighter due to the differences in exposure. I didn't purposely do any swelling tricks (that I know of). What would cause this?

posts.post_subject: Well folks, I did it!!!  My very first hologram(s)!
posts.content_md: Well, did 4 more last night. I started combining two long time passions of mine, holograms and origami... making holograms of origami subjects. They turned out pretty good, but I noticed a very slight milkyness (sp?) on the film that wasn't there on the dice holograms. The only thing I did different was that the dice holograms were brought out into the sun after the photo-flo was applied to expedite drying (although, I've recently read here that this is bad...). The dice films look slightly darker than the batch last night. The new holo's still look good, but the slight milkyness on the film tends to reflect light back at the viewer, making the image slightly harder to view. Could the sun-drying have been a benefit in this case? Or perhaps there's another cause?
